sources.label: AuditEvent model: no FKs by design

cards.title: How to read a row
items: id is a uuid primary key on all 28 tables; Python generates it (app/db/base.py:71-77), so no database extension is required and public ids are non-enumerable.
Every enum column is varchar(32) plus an explicit CHECK listing its values, never a native PostgreSQL enum: adding a value is an ordinary migration (app/db/base.py:8-11, 101-107).
Money is NUMERIC(20,4) (app/db/base.py:43) and serialises as a decimal string. No money column is floating point; ranking_score and confidence are the only floats.
A fk badge names its target as entity.attribute in the same row, and that target is checked against the declared tables. A column carrying two roles shows both badges (fk bullets uk).
Solid line = NOT NULL foreign key, so the child cannot exist without the parent. Dashed line with a circle = nullable foreign key, an optional reference.

cards.title: Enforced vs logical links
items: Every edge drawn is a foreign key the database enforces. Where a link is logical but unenforced, it is named here instead of drawn.
audit_events has no foreign keys on purpose (app/models/audit.py:49-72): organization_id, actor_user_id, entity_id and policy_version_id stay plain uuids so the event outlives the row it refers to.
policy_exceptions.subject_id is polymorphic over membership, user, expense, trip and expense_category, fixed by a CHECK, not a foreign key.
findings.rule_id is a stable string, not a foreign key, so a finding stays readable after its rule row is retired.
role_assignments.scope_id is a plain uuid indexed by scope_type: it addresses a dimension, not one table.

Four foreign keys point back at their own table and are stated here because no self-loop is drawn: departments.parent_department_id, organization_memberships.primary_manager_membership_id, receipts.parent_receipt_id and findings.superseded_by_finding_id.

The actor columns created_by_user_id, uploaded_by_user_id, granted_by_user_id, assigned_by_user_id, decided_by_user_id, validated_by_user_id, approved_by_user_id, reviewed_by_user_id and resolved_by_user_id each reference users.id. They are drawn on the column; drawing all sixteen would put sixteen ends on one side of users.
organization_id appears on 20 tables and is drawn from each of them; the hub edges bundle onto the trunk beside organizations.

cards.title: Integrity guards the database holds
items: policy_rules.source_requires_validation: is_active = true requires source_clause, validated_by_user_id, validated_at and evaluator_type (policy.py:145-153), so an invented rule cannot be activated.
allowance_profile_items.limit_requires_source: a limit_amount cannot be stored without a source_clause and a currency (organization.py:193-199).

expense_field_evidence.extraction_requires_receipt: a row claiming receipt_extraction must name the receipt. The partial unique index uq_expense_field_evidence_current allows one current row per (expense, field, is_current).
uq_duplicate_candidates_pair makes (A,B) and (B,A) one candidate; uq_findings_identity stops a re-run multiplying findings for one claim version and scope.
policy_assignments.stack: scope_selector_consistent forces exactly the selector the dimension needs, scope_key_canonical stores the canonical key, and uniqueness is over the coalesced selector.
resolution_requires_state, rejection_requires_reason and decision_requires_actor refuse a resolved finding, a rejection or an approved task without the actor and the reason.

cards.title: Append-only, and what is not claimed
items: audit_events append-only is enforced by the trigger trg_audit_events_append_only, which raises on UPDATE or DELETE before the row is touched (0001_initial_schema.py:1850-1857).
That is database-enforced behaviour, not cryptographic immutability, not WORM storage and not a legal-admissibility claim.
idempotency_keys makes a retry safe: UNIQUE(actor_user_id, idempotency_key) plus a request_hash, so the same key with a different body is refused rather than applied twice.
receipts stores only raw_text_sha256 and raw_payload_sha256; extracted text is not a column, because retention rules are unanswered (receipt.py:13-15).
Policy and rule tables ship empty, and the demo company policy is fictional, seeded only under local demo flags. No threshold here is authored policy.
extraction_runs records every attempt with provider and prompt_version; a stored run is not proof that text was extracted.
